text: Ask Claude for dashboard with tabs and charts and it feels like it just handwrites one HTML file. It doesn't. That file is bundled from a real project. So, what actually gets built first? The skill is a four-step pipeline. Step one, initialize with bash script {slash} init artifact.sh passing a project name. That one command provisions React 18 with TypeScript via Vite, Tailwind CSS 3, 4, one with Shadcn/UI theming, path aliases, more than 40 Shadcn/UI components with Radix UI and Parcel for bundling. Step two, develop by editing the generated code. Step three, bundle with bash script {slash} bundle artifact.sh. It installs Parcel and HTML and inline builds the

Project and inlines everything into one self-contained bundle HTML. Step four, share bundle HTML in the conversation. Testing is step five and it's explicitly optional. Build first, test only if issues come up or the user asks. The design section names four patterns to avoid: excessive centered layouts, purple gradients, uniform rounded corners, and turf font. That's the whole rule, negative and specific, no positive design system, so taste still does the work. The bundle itself carries React and React DOM, Tailwind utility classes, Shadcn/UI component styles, every Radix UI primitive, and whatever else your code imports collapsed into a single HTML file. The architectural insight is that init artifact.sh and bundle

Artifact.sh solve two separate problems at once, bootstrapping a real React project and collapsing it back into one shareable file. Two things worth knowing before you rely on it. Bundling requires Node 18 or higher and an index.html in the project root. Skip either and bundle artifact.sh fails. And the skill's description mentions routing support. But the init script does not install React Router. That piece isn't wired in for you. That single HTML file isn't handwritten. It's bundled from a real React project. One script provisions the stack. One script collapses it back down to a file you can share. Your turn. Paste this into Claude. Build me a note-taking app with tags, search,

A markdown editor as a shareable Claude AI artifact use the web artifacts builder. Watch four things does Claude run in an artifact SH before writing any component code. Does it use shadcn/ui components from the pre-installed set instead of writing its own UI from scratch? Does it run bundle artifact SH and share bundle HTML at the end? Not a raw index HTML or a dev server link and does the result actually avoid the four named patterns? No dominant centered layout, no purple gradient, no every corner the same radius, no inter font. Web artifacts builder Liam in for bear.
